inlines.text: The order of the Appellate Division should be affirmed.
"In the context of a Grand Jury proceeding, legal sufficiency means prima facie proof of the crimes charged, not proof beyond a reasonable doubt" (

, 92 NY2d 523, 526 [1998] [citations omitted]). "The reviewing court's inquiry is limited to whether the facts, if proven, and the inferences that logically flow from those facts supply proof of every element of the charged crimes . . . ." (

[internal quotation marks omitted].) "That other, innocent inferences could possibly be drawn from [the evidence presented to the grand jury] is irrelevant to the sufficiency inquiry where, as here, the Grand Jury could rationally have drawn the guilty inference" (
